content:
You only need to look at some of the comments here to find that a small group of people are loud, opposing all AI tools, including Apple Intelligence. This situation has given rise to an unofficial tool that allows people to disable this feature on Mac and remove all downloaded Siri AI models.

We warned yesterday that doing so may carry risks, but now some believe that to protect hardware sales, Apple may have to officially support the ability to remove AI...

Recently, opposition to generative AI has been growing louder, with opponents citing a wide range of reasons, from concerns about the survival of the human race to simply not wanting unnecessary AI features taking up device storage space.

The latest Apple Intelligence models require up to 14GB of storage space, so if you don't want these features, it's a significant burden for a 256GB device. Independent developer Om Lahore has therefore developed a project called RemoveMacAI.

Ewolf's popular comments

I've already turned off AI and Siri on all browsers on my computer and phone. It feels great to rediscover the internet experience of around 2012.

I don't want, don't need, and won't miss AI.

We warned yesterday that using this tool is not without risks. Given that Apple Intelligence is already deeply embedded in macOS 27, it may cause unwanted effects on even basic functions.

However, some believe Apple may need to provide an official method to let users remove Apple Intelligence on Mac. John Gruber of Daring Fireball mentioned that some organizations have banned the installation of AI tools.

To be clear, Apple does offer a lot of management options for organizations using device management. Apple currently says organizations can "restrict the use" of some Apple Intelligence features, and there are individual toggles to enable or disable each feature one by one. What's currently missing is a master switch that can turn off all Apple Intelligence features at once and also choose to remove downloaded models.

This issue isn't urgent for now, but when future Macs start to no longer support older versions of macOS, not giving users an easy way to remove AI models may start to affect Apple's hardware sales.
